recent_posts.title: Introducing Code Tours: a new way to review
recent_posts.summary: Graphite introduces Code Tours, a feature that transforms pull requests into guided walkthroughs of code changes. Instead of jumping between PR descriptions, comments, and diffs, reviewers get a structured narrative that combines explanation and implementation in one view. Upcoming additions include visual artifacts and test validation. Graphite is also expanding Cursor Agent access to reviewers, allowing them to run scripts, execute tests, and make tool calls directly within the review flow.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Cursor Cloud Agents in Graphite
recent_posts.summary: Graphite is launching Cursor Cloud Agents integration, allowing developers to create, review, refine, and merge AI-generated PRs entirely within the browser. A new Agents tab lets users prompt Cursor Cloud Agents directly in Graphite to generate code, produce video demos, and open draft PRs. During PR review, developers can chat with the agent inline to request changes without switching to an IDE. The integration supports multiple coding models and preserves full context whether starting in Cursor or Graphite. Available now for Cursor Pro and above users.

recent_posts.title: Building the future of software development with Cursor
recent_posts.summary: Graphite, a code review platform, has signed an agreement to join Cursor, an AI-powered development tool. The acquisition aims to create an integrated platform for AI-assisted code creation, review, and merging. Graphite will continue operating independently while building deeper integrations with Cursor, combining their AI reviewer capabilities, and accelerating their vision of collaborative human-agent development workflows. The deal addresses the emerging bottleneck in software development where AI enables rapid code generation but review processes haven't kept pace.

recent_posts.title: Reimagining the PR Page: Designing for speed and focus
recent_posts.summary: Graphite rebuilt their PR page to reduce visual clutter and improve code review focus. Key additions include a rich text editor for more accessible commenting (removing markdown barriers for non-technical collaborators) and floating comments that keep discussion threads visible without disrupting the diff view. The team experimented with moving the PR stack to a sidebar but ultimately kept it in a horizontal layout for better readability. The redesign prioritized iterative development through internal dogfooding to create a faster, more intuitive review experience.

recent_posts.title: Graphite changelog [11-20-2025]
recent_posts.summary: Graphite released a major redesign of their pull request page with improved navigation, rich text editing, and streamlined code review workflows. Key updates include a left-aligned file tree, top-positioned version navigation, inline action cards for resolving conflicts, comments positioned to the right of code diffs, and a unified CI job details panel. The redesign aims to reduce visual clutter and align with developer review patterns for faster, more efficient code reviews.

recent_posts.title: Graphite changelog [11-04-2025]
recent_posts.summary: Graphite has migrated from graphite.dev to graphite.com. Users need to sign in again on first visit, update Slack app permissions for link unfurling, and can now swap github.com with graphite.com in PR URLs to open them directly in Graphite. The domain change reflects the platform's evolution from a dev tool to an AI-powered code review platform.

recent_posts.title: Graphite changelog [10-16-2025]
recent_posts.summary: Graphite announces major product updates including Graphite Agent, which unifies AI code review and chat capabilities into a single pull request experience. The platform now offers a streamlined workflow for creating, reviewing, and merging code with stack-aware features. New simplified pricing tiers include a free Hobby plan, $20/user Starter plan, and $40/user Team plan with a 30-day trial. CLI version 1.7.1 adds new commands for commit authorship control, upstack/downstack deletion options, and various bug fixes for improved terminal compatibility.

recent_posts.title: Students embrace collaborative AI-powered development at Hack the North 2025
recent_posts.summary: Hack the North 2025 showcased how students are embracing collaborative, AI-powered development tools. Graphite sponsored the event with a Dream Team award recognizing teams using stacked PRs and their platform. Students leveraged AI coding assistants like Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and Claude Code, while Graphite provided structured code review capabilities to ensure quality. The event demonstrated how emerging developers are combining AI assistance with human oversight, learning essential collaboration skills and modern workflows that will define the future of software engineering.

recent_posts.title: Graphite launches Agent to unify AI code review and chat features
recent_posts.summary: Graphite announces Graphite Agent, unifying their AI reviewer (Diamond) and Chat features into a single AI code review experience. Unlike traditional AI reviewers that only provide comments, Graphite Agent acts as a collaborative tool that reviews, edits, and helps merge PRs directly within the pull request interface. The company is integrating AI capabilities into all pricing tiers, with new plans starting at free for individuals, $20 for Starter, and $40 for Team (including unlimited AI reviews). All plans include a 30-day free trial without requiring a credit card, and existing customers will transition to new plans after January 8, 2026.

recent_posts.title: Introducing frozen branches: A safer way to build on your teammates’ work
recent_posts.summary: Graphite introduces frozen branches in version 1.7.0, a new feature that allows developers to safely build on teammates' work without accidentally modifying their branches. Frozen branches automatically stay read-only when pulled down using 'gt get', preventing accidental edits while still allowing remote updates and new branches to be built on top. This feature reduces collaboration friction by protecting against merge conflicts and overwrites in shared development workflows.
